answer: A lagoon stays healthy when its waters move, so let standing flow through rotating savings circles. Each identity joins a circle of strangers, pays a fixed stake each epoch, and takes turns receiving the payout. Three members must stake their standing on the newcomer's uniqueness. If a member is proven a duplicate, its stake is forfeited and sponsors lose standing too. One operator running many identities must fund many streams; like a falcon that cannot hunt two distant karst valleys at once, it cannot keep every circle alive, so each clone costs as much as the last.
